title: CHAPTER TWENTY. Christian warfare: enemies
latin: CAPUT VIGESIMUM, De militia et cruce Christiana. Militia Christiana est pugna spiritualis fidelium adversus hostes salutis sub duce Christo. II. Discernendi Dei hostes: IV. Satan est hostis Dei inde a principio. IV. Mundus principem suum secutus Deo et amicis Dei inimicatur (James 4:4; John 15:18-19). V. Caro nostra Deo et Spiritui eius adversa est (Gal. 5:16-17; Rom. 8:5-7).
english: CHAPTER TWENTY. On Christian warfare and the cross.
Christian warfare is believers' spiritual fight against the enemies of salvation under Christ the captain.
God's enemies to be distinguished: Satan from the beginning; the world following its prince and hating God and His friends; our flesh opposed to God and His Spirit.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): God's enemies toward be distinguished: Satan from ye beginning; ye world following its prince and hating God and His friends; our flesh opposed toward God and His Spirit. — Christian warfare stands as believers' spiritual fight against ye enemies belonging toward salvation under Christ ye captain. — CHAPTER TWENTY. On Christian warfare and ye cross.

title: Christ the captain; victory applied in members
latin: VI–VII. Quamvis Satanas consilium Dei de salute impedire conatus sit, Pater misit Filium ut quod perierat servaret et opera diaboli destrueret (Gen. 3:15; 1 John 3:8). Dux militiae Christianae Christus hostem in cruce ac morte impugnavit et vicit. VIII. Victoria a Christo capite in diebus carnis peracta corporaliter, a Christianis membris spiritualiter per fidem et Spiritum applicatur et continuatur.
english: VI–VII. Though Satan tried to hinder God's counsel of salvation, the Father sent the Son to save what was lost and destroy the devil's works. Christ the captain assaulted and conquered the enemy in the cross and death.
VIII. The victory accomplished bodily by Christ the Head in the days of His flesh is applied and continued spiritually in Christian members through faith and the Spirit.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): VIII. Ye victory accomplished bodily by Christ ye Head in ye days belonging toward His flesh stands as applied and continued spiritually in Christian members through faith and ye Spirit. — VI–VII. Though Satan tried toward hinder God's counsel belonging toward salvation, ye Father sent ye Son toward save what stood as lost and destroy ye devil's works. Christ ye captain assaulted and conquered ye enemy in ye cross and death.

title: Armor; novitiate; prize
latin: X. Arma militiae promunt Apostolus Eph. 6:10ff.—lorica iustitiae, scutum fidei, galea salutis, gladius Spiritus. XI–XII. Tirones adversus manifesta opera carnis et occultas cordis improbitates. XVII. Brabeum victoribus paratum est arbor vitae, corona vitae, nomen novum (Rev. 2).
english: X. The Apostle sets out the armor (Eph. 6)—breastplate of righteousness, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, sword of the Spirit.
XI–XII. Recruits fight both open works of the flesh and hidden heart-wickedness. XVII. The prize prepared for conquerors is the tree of life, the crown of life, the new name.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): XI–XII. Recruits fight both open works belonging toward ye flesh and hidden heart-wickedness. XVII. Ye prize prepared for conquerors stands as ye tree belonging toward life, ye crown belonging toward life, ye new name. — X. Ye Apostle sets out ye armor (Eph. 6)—breastplate belonging toward righteousness, shield belonging toward faith, helmet belonging toward salvation, sword belonging toward ye Spirit.

title: The cross: school of life; medicine; heaviest conflict
latin: Crux fidelium: 1. Schola crucis est schola lucis. 2. Quamvis peccata fidelium crucem ut poenam per se mereantur, a Deo vertitur in medicinam. 3. Crux omnium gravissima est ubi fidelis anima cum ipso Deo tanquam hoste committitur—tentatio derelictionis—quae tamen fide vincitur. CAPUT VIGESIMUM PRIMUM sequitur, De precatione.
english: On the believers' cross: 1. The school of the cross is the school of light. 2. Though believers' sins deserve the cross as punishment, God turns it into medicine.
3. The heaviest cross is when the faithful soul is engaged with God Himself as if an enemy—the trial of forsakenness—yet conquered by faith.
pass_a: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TWENTY-ONE follows, On prayer. — 3. Ye heaviest cross stands as when ye faithful soul stands as engaged with God Himself as if an enemy—the trial belonging toward forsakenness—yet conquered by faith. — On ye believers' cross: 1. Ye school belonging toward ye cross stands as ye school belonging toward light. 2. Though believers' sins deserve ye cross as punishment, God turns it into medicine.
